Per sport (BR-Q3.1): the re-entered sport reads executed history, the other x's return plus the reducer (T1, T2, T17, T19, R2 = full re-entry for running). No P34_* switch, process.env read, ANY or M path exists in CoachingCore/src at 1978cc4 (git grep). Exceptions, each a finding: BR-Q4.1 for the race touch's completion rule (SSCTR-P34R-F02); BR-Q4.4 for a race week whose only required runs are the touch and the race (SSCTR-P34R-F03); BR-Q1.3 for a question met inside x's own stop, the first-day strength ambiguity (SSCTR-P34R-F04); and the guard of BR-Q1.2(f) misfiring on a corrected latest break (SSCTR-P34R-F01, under Q2).

findings.cause: Code reading: appliedBetween(ctx, x.end, start) is true for any recorded episode with live.end > x.end and live.start < start. On the re-read of a corrected latest break (recordedStop, then stopOf), the corrected break's own episode is on record, applied by the first return, with its old start (Mon wk6) before the corrected start (Tue wk6), so it is read as an applied return between the holiday and the stop. A correction that keeps or moves the start earlier does not reach it, which is why T21 passes.
findings.closure: Only a return of another episode can be an applied return between the breaks: the episode of the break being read (the latest break, whose report is being corrected) is never counted by the guard. Expected: C5 equals C5f in stop, class, separateBreaks, run and strength doses; T21's week-moved-in case, once its unreported week is answered, never reads continuity because of the corrected break's own earlier report; T20's guard case (another break C applied between) still blocks the own return.
findings.authority: BR-Q1.2(f) (the guard is about an applied return between x and S), CF-P34-02, the Q7 addendum ruling (a named correction supersedes only the report it corrects), I9. No number.

findings.class: IMPLEMENTATION_FIDELITY_DEFECT (BR-Q4.4 and INTERFACE-6 section 1; the inverse direction; the registered P18(c) flags it)
findings.finding: Running re-enters only through a week holding at least one gated run row, because the reducer's complete('RUN') needs a gate key. A race week whose runs are the race touch, an optional shakeout and the race (run days Thu, Sat, Sun with a Sunday race) holds two required run sessions under BR-Q4.1, and BR-Q4.4 lets a sport re-enter through any week holding at least one required session. Executed in full, it never re-enters running: in a run-only plan the stop runs through the earlier break (the inverse defect direction A closes), in a hybrid plan running reads the earlier break's own return instead of its executed history.

findings.class: IMPLEMENTATION_FIDELITY_DEFECT (BR-Q1.3 'a decision met inside it is returned'; rule 0.8; an existing question dropped)
findings.finding: When the earlier break x is read as its own return and strength reads from it (strength not re-entered), a strength session logged on x's first day without a stated start time is ordered by default (as after the start) without the question rule 0.8 asks when the order changes the state the return starts from. ownReturnOf computes the state's material flag and drops it. The two readings give different strength prescriptions, so the return guesses where the existing rule asks.
findings.reproduction: probes/p34-recheck.mjs. SD1 (V1 shape; the Monday wk2 lift on A's first day reported executed, no startedAt): candidate REESTABLISH, SHORT 4, OWN_RETURN, strength back-squat 1x7 ESTABLISH, db lifts 1x12 FROM_LOG. SD2 (the same with A's start stated after the lift, so the lift counts): back-squat 1x9 ESTABLISH, db lifts 1x8 FROM_LOG. SD1k (A alone, by a return report): ASK interruption.startedAt on both runtimes. SD1 on R7D-FREEZE-4 (continuity): ASK interruption.startedAt. SD3 (V2 shape, strength complete, the same lift): no question on the candidate, which is right, because strength reads its executed history and the order does not change the state.
findings.closure: When the sport read from x's own return includes strength (STRENGTH not re-entered) and x's own stop's state is material (stateAtBreak.material, the existing test), the return asks for x's start time (interruption.startedAt, naming x's episodeId), as rule 0.8 asks on the single-break path; recursively for an inner own return. Expected: SD1 ASK with interruption.startedAt, nothing applied; SD2 and SD3 unchanged; V1 without the lift unchanged.
findings.authority: BR-Q1.3, rule 0.8 and R7-A.2 section 5 (the order of a first-day session is asked when material), I9 ('asked, never guessed'). No number.

observations.note: Race weeks: when running is not re-entered (W2-W4, RT3: the touch or race missed, or an adverse touch) the candidate projects week 9 at EASY 35/35 and LONG 45, above W1's full re-entry (EASY 35/34, LONG 40) and above R7D-FREEZE-4 on those paths. It equals the existing episode rule on the same facts (EPW1 and EPW3, the holiday applied when stated: EASY 35/35, LONG 45 with the race done or missed), within the prior tolerated doses and the single-run ceiling. The cause is the interaction of the existing return ladder with the post-event block, not this candidate's logic. Disclose; if the Founder or PCG want the post-event rules to bound a return ladder after a race, that is a separate question. No dose judgment is made here.

The reducer's step release ignores the race keys (they hold no gate): a race week with the race or touch missed still releases a run step on its executed easy runs (EPW3 equals EPW1). Pre-existing and outside this phase; BR-Q4 binds re-entry only, so the candidate is right not to change it. Route only if step release should follow the re-entry contract on race weeks.

With SSCTR-P34R-F02 fixed, P18(a) can count a race touch or race as executed only when its report is not PARTIAL and stay a necessary condition of the runtime; that would detect the F02 shape. See CFR-05.
The five updated assertions are correct from the domain side; the phase32 T5 title's 'corrects its facts' asserts nothing observable (cosmetic).

Shapes that pass and are worth keeping: X9 (three breaks, inner own return), G6 (executed runs of the return's own week still count in the ceiling), F1/F2/F2b/F2c (R-F08-1 on separate-break paths), F3 (nonclinical control).

aeReview.2_materialFact: Yes: the declared breaks, the executed sessions with their completion and responses, and the corrected report, all on the append-only record.
aeReview.3_keepDefensible: KEEP of 1978cc4 as frozen is not defensible while the four defects stand; KEEP of direction A is.
aeReview.4_changeNecessary: Yes, narrowly: four predicates read the existing rules incompletely.
aeReview.5_smallestIntervention: Four runtime-only predicate fixes (guard excludes the corrected episode; completion rule for the race touch; touch and race as required sessions for a week without gated runs; the 0.8 question inside x's own stop), no number.
aeReview.6_smallerAlternatives: Disclosure alone leaves a restart on the mandatory case (F01), an F01-direction re-entry (F02), a registered-oracle failure (F03) and an unasked guess (F04). Changing the instruments instead would weaken the oracle.
aeReview.7_priorityAndProgression: The fixes restore BR-Q3 per-sport progression and the earlier breaks' effects; none raises a dose above the executed record.
aeReview.8_evidenceSupportsDose: Unchanged approved R6 recipes and the decision's directional claims (CL1-CL6, SUPPORTED_WITH_LIMITS, abstracts only), relied on as recorded.
aeReview.9_uncertainty: Frequency of these shapes in real use (corrections of trip dates are common; touch-only race weeks and same-day lifts less so). Group means only.
aeReview.10_askHoldClinical: ASK for the first-day order (F04) and unknown training between; CLINICAL_HUMAN_REQUIRED for every clinical-cause episode (R-F08-1 holds); F08 stays clinical and blocked by authority.

conditionsForFreeze.condition: Close SSCTR-P34R-F01 to F04 in the one bounded runtime-only cycle, each with its closure as stated in the finding, with a directed test per finding that fails on 1978cc4 and passes after (C5; RT1o and RT1; RWo and RW; SD1 with SD2 and SD3 as controls). Change nothing else: T1-T21, the five updated assertions, the conformance anchors (R7-B, R7-B.1, R7-B.2) and every other case of p34-ssctr.mjs, p34-ceiling.mjs and p34-recheck.mjs keep their 1978cc4 outputs in this folder.

Closure is objective: on the corrected candidate, probes/p34-recheck.mjs gives C5 = C5f; RT1o = RT2o; RT1 = OWN_RETURN with RUN null and STRENGTH re-entered; RWo and RW = TRAINING_AFTER, SHORT 4; SD1 = ASK interruption.startedAt with nothing applied; and probes/p34-recheck-detectors.mjs shows P18(c) not flagging RWo. If every expectation holds and nothing else changed, the Quality narrow check and Chief can verify it and the domain position on the corrected candidate becomes ACCEPT_WITH_CONDITIONS (CFR-03 to CFR-06) without another full SSCTR review. Any deviation, or any other behaviour change, returns to a fresh SSCTR instance for these items only. If the cycle does not close them, no freeze: the phase closes with the open findings named.
